sirt_reconstruct — TOMOGRAPHY ct_scan op

• Data kinds: projstack × ctgeometry → voxel

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sirt_reconstruct(projections, geometry, n_iter=50, relaxation=1.0, initial=None, nonnegative=True, device='auto', on_iter=None) (to call the implementation directly, import ctscan; ctscan.sirt_reconstruct(projections, geometry, n_iter=50, relaxation=1.0, initial=None, nonnegative=True, device='auto', on_iter=None); from the registry, opstomography.get("sirt_reconstruct"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

SIRT: every view at once, x <- x + lam C A^T R (p - A x).

R and C are the inverse row and column sums of A. With the matched pair of this family it minimises a weighted least-squares error, and it needs no formula, so it is the route for tomosynthesis, few views and limited angle.

:param projections: (view, V, U) line integrals. :param geometry: dict from ct_scan_geometry. :param n_iter: iterations, 1 .. 5000. :param relaxation: step lam, (0, 2). :param initial: starting volume; None gives zeros. :param nonnegative: clip to >= 0 after each iteration. :param device: "auto", "cpu" or "cuda". :param on_iter: optional on_iter(iteration, volume) for a convergence curve. :returns: (Z, Y, X) float volume. :raises ValueError: on a shape that disagrees with the geometry or a relaxation

outside (0, 2). Empty input (projections with 0 elements) raises

ValueError.
